research.title: ATOC’s Greenland campaign features in the PBS series “Ages of Ice”
research.people: Sebastian Schmidt’s group · Vikas Nataraja and Ken Hirata
research.blurb: ARCSIX, the NASA airborne campaign over Greenland led by Sebastian Schmidt, appears in episode two of Ages of Ice. Vikas Nataraja and Ken Hirata supported the mission in the field — pictured with the ARCSIX sticker they had just added to a hangar door, a campaign tradition, and with NASA’s P-3 after some work on the group’s sensors. “Polar Seas” airs Wednesday, September 23 at 10 p.m. ET on PBS, the PBS app, and PBS’s YouTube channel. #AgesofIce

colloquia._readme: Past dates disappear on their own, so it is safe to paste in the whole semester. Date must be YYYY-MM-DD. "image" is optional — a flyer in images/ shows beside the details.
colloquia.speaker: Dr. Scott Doney
colloquia.title: Marine Carbon Dioxide Removal
colloquia.abstract: Stabilizing global climate will likely require removing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere as well as cutting emissions. Ocean-based approaches show promise, but none is ready to deploy at scale: gaps remain in efficacy, permanence, verification, cost, and governance.

colloquia.speaker: Jelle Schrijver
colloquia.title: A Methane Plume Seen from Space: What Can We Actually Measure?
colloquia.abstract: Satellites can now resolve methane plumes from individual point sources at scales of tens of metres. Turning an observed plume into an emission rate is far harder: both the retrieval and the atmospheric transport carry uncertainty. This talk covers a physics-based optimal-estimation retrieval, how differences between instruments affect what counts as a detection, and work using large-eddy simulation against controlled-release experiments to pin down how wind and turbulence limit satellite-derived emission estimates.

colloquia.speaker: Dr. Lynn Harvey (LASP) and Dr. Laura Holt (NWRA)
colloquia.title: Cora Randall: A career of scientific vision, community, and deep humanity
colloquia.tag: In honor of Prof. Cora Randall
colloquia.abstract: Cora Randall’s research on the energetic particle precipitation indirect effect showed how nitrogen oxides made high in the atmosphere descend through the winter polar vortex to alter stratospheric ozone. She led the AIM/CIPS investigation of polar mesospheric clouds and the WAVE DRIVE Science Center. This colloquium celebrates both the science and the person — teacher, mentor, department chair, and extraordinarily generous colleague.

colloquia.speaker: Dr. Kirsten Mayer
colloquia.title: Investigating Subseasonal Predictability with Earth System Models and Machine Learning
colloquia.abstract: Machine learning for subseasonal forecasting is data-limited: the observational record holds too few examples of the climate states that give rise to predictability to train a model on. This talk looks at how Earth system models can fill that gap, and how explainable AI and emulators can be used to find the sources of subseasonal predictability, including recent progress on NSF NCAR’s emulator work. Conversation from 10:45 AM.
